messages.content: How far will a car travel in time 't' when launched with velocity 'v' at an angle 'theta'?

function.name: calculate_projectile_range
function.description: Calculate the range of a projectile launched at an angle with initial velocity, using the kinematic equation. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

initial_velocity.description: The initial velocity at which projectile is launched. This is a float type value.

angle.description: The angle at which projectile is launched. This should be in degrees. This is a float type value.

time.description: The time in seconds after which the range is to be calculated. This is a float type value.

message.reasoning: The user asks: "How far will a car travel in time 't' when launched with velocity 'v' at an angle 'theta'?" They want distance traveled in time t given initial velocity v and launch angle theta. This is a projectile motion problem. The range formula: R = (v^2 * sin(2θ)) / g. But that's total horizontal distance after landing. But they ask "in time t". So horizontal distance traveled in time t: x(t) = v * cos(theta) * t. If we consider vertical motion too? But distance traveled along trajectory: s(t) = v * t (if no acceleration). But if projectile under gravity, horizontal component constant, vertical component changes. The path length is integral of speed: sqrt((v cosθ)^2 + (v sinθ - g t)^2) dt. That integral yields something. But likely they want horizontal distance: v cosθ * t. So answer: distance = v * cos(theta) * t. If they want range formula: R = (v^2 sin(2θ))/g. But they mention time t. So use horizontal distance. Provide explanation. Also mention g=9.81 m/s^2. Provide formula. Also mention if t is time until landing: t = 2 v sinθ / g. Then R = v cosθ * t. So answer: R = v cosθ * t. Provide numeric example.
